fact.en:
Do magnets attract all metals?

No! Magnets only attract objects made of iron, cobalt, and nickel. Other metals like gold and copper are not magnetic.
fact.tl:
Lahat ba ng metal ay naa-attract ng magnet?

Hindi! Ang magnet ay nakaka-attract lang ng mga bagay na gawa sa iron, cobalt, at nickel. Ang ibang metal tulad ng ginto at tanso ay hindi magnetic.
fact.bis:
Ang tanang metal ba ma-attract sa magnet?

Dili! Ang magnet maka-attract lang ug mga butang nga hinimo sa iron, cobalt, ug nickel. Ang uban nga metal sama sa bulawan ug tumbaga dili magnetic.

cards.illustration: A bar magnet held near a pile of mixed objects, pulling only a nail and a nickel coin while ignoring a gold ring and a copper wire.

fact.en: Magnets come in different shapes, including ring, rectangular, horseshoe, and bar magnets.
fact.tl: May iba't ibang hugis ang magnet, tulad ng ring, rectangular, horseshoe, at bar magnets.
fact.bis: Ang mga magnet adunay lain-laing porma, sama sa ring, rectangular, horseshoe, ug bar magnets.

cards.illustration: Four different magnets laid out on a table: a ring, a rectangle, a U-shaped horseshoe, and a straight bar.

fact.en: Every magnet has two ends called poles: one is the north pole and the other is the south pole.
fact.tl: Ang bawat magnet ay may dalawang dulo na tinatawag na poles: ang isa ay north pole at ang isa ay south pole.
fact.bis: Ang matag magnet adunay duha ka tumoy nga gitawag ug poles: ang usa mao ang north pole ug ang usa mao ang south pole.

cards.illustration: A bar magnet with one end painted red and marked N, and the other end painted blue and marked S.

fact.en:
What happens if you cut a magnet in half?

You get two new magnets! Each piece will have its own north pole and south pole.
fact.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kung hatiin mo ang isang magnet sa dalawa?

Magkakaroon ka ng dalawang bagong magnet! Ang bawat piraso ay magkakaroon ng sarili nitong north pole at south pole.
fact.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo kung putlon nimo ang usa ka magnet sa tunga?

Makakuha ka ug duha ka bag-ong magnet! Ang matag piraso adunay kaugalingong north pole ug south pole.

cards.illustration: A bar magnet broken into two pieces, with each smaller piece showing its own N and S poles.

fact.en: Magnetic force is the push or pull that a magnet exerts on certain objects.
fact.tl: Ang magnetic force ay ang pagtulak o paghila na ginagawa ng magnet sa ilang mga bagay.
fact.bis: Ang magnetic force mao ang pagtulod o pagbira nga gihimo sa magnet sa pipila ka mga butang.

cards.illustration: A hand holding a magnet that is pulling a paper clip towards it, with small arrows showing the direction of the pull.

fact.en:
What happens when two north poles face each other?

They push each other away! Like magnetic poles repel each other.
fact.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kapag nagkaharap ang dalawang north pole?

Nagtutulakan sila palayo! Ang magkaparehong magnetic poles ay nagre-repel sa isa't isa.
fact.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo kung mag-atubang ang duha ka north pole?

Magtulod sila palayo! Ang managsamang magnetic poles mag-repel sa usag usa.

cards.illustration: Two bar magnets with their north poles facing each other, with arrows showing them being pushed apart.

fact.en:
Why do a north pole and a south pole stick together?

Because unlike magnetic poles attract each other! They pull towards one another.
fact.tl:
Bakit nagdidikit ang north pole at south pole?

Dahil ang magkaibang magnetic poles ay nag-a-attract sa isa't isa! Hinihila nila ang isa't isa.
fact.bis:
Ngano nga magtapot ang north pole ug south pole?

Tungod kay ang managlahing magnetic poles mag-attract sa usag usa! Magbira sila paingon sa usag usa.

cards.illustration: Two bar magnets with a north pole and a south pole facing each other, with arrows showing them being pulled together.

fact.en: A magnet's force is strongest at its poles and weaker in the middle.
fact.tl: Ang lakas ng magnet ay pinakamalakas sa mga poles nito at mas mahina sa gitna.
fact.bis: Ang kusog sa magnet pinakalig-on sa mga poles niini ug mas huyang sa tunga.

cards.illustration: A bar magnet with many paper clips clinging to its two ends and only one paper clip weakly attached in the middle.

fact.en: A magnetic field is the area around a magnet where its magnetic force can act.
fact.tl: Ang magnetic field ay ang lugar sa paligid ng magnet kung saan kumikilos ang kanyang magnetic force.
fact.bis: Ang magnetic field mao ang lugar sa palibot sa magnet diin molihok ang iyang magnetic force.

cards.illustration: A bar magnet with curved lines looping from its north pole to its south pole, showing the invisible field around it.

fact.en:
Does a magnet get weaker when it is far away?

Yes! The magnetic field strength decreases with distance from the magnet.
fact.tl:
Humihina ba ang magnet kapag malayo ito?

Oo! Ang lakas ng magnetic field ay bumababa habang lumalayo sa magnet.
fact.bis:
Mohuyang ba ang magnet kung layo kini?

Oo! Ang kusog sa magnetic field mokunhod samtang molayo sa magnet.

cards.illustration: A magnet with a paper clip close to it being pulled strongly, and another paper clip farther away not being pulled at all.

fact.en: Magnetic force can act through some non-magnetic materials such as plastic, wood, and paper.
fact.tl: Ang magnetic force ay kayang dumaan sa ilang non-magnetic materials tulad ng plastic, kahoy, at papel.
fact.bis: Ang magnetic force makaagi sa pipila ka non-magnetic materials sama sa plastic, kahoy, ug papel.

cards.illustration: A hand holding a magnet above a wooden table, with a paper clip on the underside of the table being held up by the magnetic force.

fact.en:
Can anything block a magnet's force?

Yes! A piece of iron can block or cut the magnetic force, stopping it from reaching other objects.
fact.tl:
May makakaharang ba sa lakas ng magnet?

Oo! Ang isang piraso ng bakal ay kayang harangin o putulin ang magnetic force, kaya hindi na ito makakaabot sa ibang bagay.
fact.bis:
Aduna bay makababag sa kusog sa magnet?

Oo! Ang usa ka piraso sa puthaw makababag o makaputol sa magnetic force, mao nga dili na kini makaabot sa laing butang.

cards.illustration: A magnet on one side of an iron plate, with paper clips on the other side lying flat and unmoved.

fact.en: Objects made of iron, cobalt, and nickel are attracted to magnets.
fact.tl: Ang mga bagay na gawa sa iron, cobalt, at nickel ay naa-attract sa magnet.
fact.bis: Ang mga butang nga hinimo sa iron, cobalt, ug nickel ma-attract sa magnet.

cards.illustration: Three objects labeled iron, cobalt, and nickel being pulled towards a large magnet.

fact.en:
Are gold and copper attracted to magnets?

No! Gold and copper are metals, but they are not magnetic. Magnets do not attract all metals.
fact.tl:
Naa-attract ba ng magnet ang ginto at tanso?

Hindi! Ang ginto at tanso ay mga metal, pero hindi sila magnetic. Hindi lahat ng metal ay naa-attract ng magnet.
fact.bis:
Ma-attract ba sa magnet ang bulawan ug tumbaga?

Dili! Ang bulawan ug tumbaga mga metal, apan dili kini magnetic. Dili tanang metal ma-attract sa magnet.

cards.illustration: A magnet held near a gold ring and a copper wire, with both objects staying still and not moving towards the magnet.

cards.topic: Magnetic Force is a Push or Pull

fact.en: The push and pull of a magnet is called magnetic force.
fact.tl: Ang pagtulak at paghila ng magnet ay tinatawag na magnetic force.
fact.bis: Ang pagtulod ug pagbira sa magnet gitawag ug magnetic force.

cards.illustration: A hand using a magnet to push one magnet away and pull another magnet closer, with arrows showing both directions.

fact.en: A horseshoe magnet is shaped like the letter U, with its two poles close together.
fact.tl: Ang horseshoe magnet ay hugis letrang U, na magkalapit ang dalawang poles nito.
fact.bis: Ang horseshoe magnet porma sama sa letra nga U, nga magtapad ang duha ka poles niini.

cards.illustration: A U-shaped magnet with its two poles pointing upward, holding a small nail on each end.

fact.en: A ring magnet is a round magnet with a hole in the center, like a donut.
fact.tl: Ang ring magnet ay bilog na magnet na may butas sa gitna, parang donut.
fact.bis: Ang ring magnet usa ka lingin nga magnet nga adunay lungag sa tunga, sama sa donut.

cards.illustration: A donut-shaped magnet with a hole in the middle, with a pencil passing through the hole.

fact.en: A bar magnet is a straight, rectangular magnet with a north pole at one end and a south pole at the other.
fact.tl: Ang bar magnet ay tuwid at rectangular na magnet na may north pole sa isang dulo at south pole sa kabilang dulo.
fact.bis: Ang bar magnet usa ka tul-id ug rectangular nga magnet nga adunay north pole sa usa ka tumoy ug south pole sa pikas tumoy.

cards.illustration: A straight rectangular magnet with one end painted red and the other blue, with N and S marked on each end.

fact.en:
Where is a magnet's force the strongest?

At its poles! The magnetic field is strongest near the poles and gets weaker as you move away.
fact.tl:
Saan pinakamalakas ang lakas ng magnet?

Sa kanyang mga poles! Ang magnetic field ay pinakamalakas malapit sa poles at humihina habang lumalayo.
fact.bis:
Asa pinakalig-on ang kusog sa magnet?

Sa iyang mga poles! Ang magnetic field pinakalig-on duol sa poles ug mohuyang samtang molayo.

cards.illustration: A bar magnet with many paper clips attached to its ends and only a few in the middle, showing the stronger force at the poles.

fact.en: A magnet can pull a paper clip even when a piece of paper is placed between them.
fact.tl: Kayang hilahin ng magnet ang paper clip kahit may papel sa pagitan nila.
fact.bis: Mabira sa magnet ang paper clip bisan pa adunay papel sa tunga nila.

cards.illustration: A magnet on top of a piece of paper, with a paper clip underneath the paper being held up by the magnetic force.

fact.en: Magnetic force can pass through a wooden ruler to attract a paper clip on the other side.
fact.tl: Ang magnetic force ay kayang dumaan sa kahoy na ruler para ma-attract ang paper clip sa kabilang side.
fact.bis: Ang magnetic force makaagi sa kahoy nga ruler aron ma-attract ang paper clip sa pikas nga kilid.

cards.illustration: A magnet held on one side of a wooden ruler, with a paper clip sticking to the other side of the ruler.

fact.en: A magnet can attract a paper clip through a plastic ruler because magnetic force passes through plastic.
fact.tl: Kayang ma-attract ng magnet ang paper clip sa pamamagitan ng plastic ruler dahil dumadaan ang magnetic force sa plastic.
fact.bis: Maka-attract ang magnet ug paper clip pinaagi sa plastic ruler tungod kay moagi ang magnetic force sa plastic.

cards.illustration: A magnet held on one side of a clear plastic ruler, with a paper clip sticking to the other side of the ruler.

fact.en: Iron can block or cut magnetic force, preventing it from attracting objects on the other side.
fact.tl: Ang bakal ay kayang harangin o putulin ang magnetic force, kaya hindi na ito makaka-attract ng mga bagay sa kabilang side.
fact.bis: Ang puthaw makababag o makaputol sa magnetic force, mao nga dili na kini maka-attract sa mga butang sa pikas nga kilid.

cards.illustration: A magnet on one side of an iron plate, with paper clips on the other side lying flat and unmoved.

fact.en: Magnets are used in everyday objects like refrigerator doors, speakers, and magnetic toys.
fact.tl: Ginagamit ang magnet sa mga pang-araw-araw na bagay tulad ng pinto ng refrigerator, speakers, at magnetic toys.
fact.bis: Gigamit ang magnet sa adlaw-adlaw nga mga butang sama sa pultahan sa refrigerator, speakers, ug magnetic toys.

cards.illustration: A refrigerator door with several colorful magnets holding papers and photos, with a speaker and a magnetic toy nearby.
